name: MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
problem: Growing cloud cost and latency concerns push LLMs on-device, which means sub-billion parameters, a scale where prevailing belief says data and parameter quantity dominate model quality.
mechanism: ARCHITECTURE rather than data, on the explicit finding that architecture matters more at sub-billion scale. Uses DEEP AND THIN architectures (many layers, few channels) plus EMBEDDING SHARING and GROUPED-QUERY ATTENTION (GQA). Also proposes an immediate BLOCK-WISE WEIGHT-SHARING scheme with no increase in model size and only marginal latency overhead, yielding the MobileLLM-LS variants.
speedup_reported: 2.7%/4.3% accuracy boost over preceding 125M/350M state-of-the-art models. Block-wise weight sharing (MobileLLM-LS) adds a further 0.7%/0.8% over MobileLLM 125M/350M, at the stated cost of NO model-size increase and only MARGINAL LATENCY OVERHEAD. Baselines are the previous sub-billion SOTA models. No tok/s figure is given in the abstract, so the accuracy deltas are what is recorded.
notes: ADOPTION: weights and code are open (open_weights true) and the models are on-device artifacts, so this is deployed as a model family even though the architectural recipe is not a serving-engine feature. VENUE: ICML 2024, corroborated by the arXiv comment field ('ICML 2024. Code is available at ...') - so venue rests on the primary source. WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE INFERENCE SLICE SPECIFICALLY: GQA is the mechanism that cuts KV-cache size and decode-time KV bandwidth per token, which is the exact resource that constrains decode; the paper attributes its gains partly to GQA rather than treating it as a training trick. The block-wise weight-sharing contribution is the more unusual idea - reusing the same weights across blocks to get accuracy without parameters or meaningful latency - and it is the one with no upstream-engine equivalent. Deployed on phones means the relevant hardware is mobile SoCs, which the repo's accelerator list may not cover, so hardware_relevance names the datacenter part used for training-side experiments rather than claiming a mobile accelerator id.
